- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days, then underestimates later days — adjust downward in early forecast windows.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — reduce forecast peak magnitude by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — force forecast to align with recent 7–10 day average if price drops >10% from peak.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often dips below forecast by day 10–15 — apply a 2–3 day lag correction for downward trends.
- If true outcome shows sustained decline after a peak, model fails to recognize it — add a “sustained decline” heuristic: if 3 consecutive days drop >2% from prior, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day.
- No sentiment signal present → model ignores macro context → assume no sentiment-driven volatility → apply conservative smoothing (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast.
